findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4856 is the community 'Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure', not an NSX add-on. The VMware NSX-T Splunk App is 4241. The wrong ID repeats in dataSources, detailedImplementation and references, and in the grounding guide.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Splunkbase 4241 (VMware NSX-T Splunk App), and note that it is syslog-based; REST transport-node polling needs a custom input.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Universal Forwarder is not supported on VMware ESXi, so scripted inputs cannot run on the host. esxcli statistics must be collected remotely (SSH, PowerCLI/vSphere API from a collector host) or through vCenter performance counters. The 'Deploy scripted probes (inputs.conf)' prerequisite has the same problem.
findings.quote: Wrap **`esxcli network nic stats`** and **`nsxdp-cli`** netcpa stats inside Universal Forwarder scripts posting newline JSON into `index=vmware`
findings.suggested_fix: Describe a remote collector (for example a Heavy Forwarder or a script host running PowerCLI Get-EsxCli or the vSphere API) that polls NIC statistics per host and sends them to HEC as esxi:nic:stats.

findings.explanation: The netcpa agent was replaced by nsx-proxy/nsx-cfgagent in NSX-T 2.4+, and 'nsxdp-cli netcpa stats' and these counter names could not be found in NSX documentation. They look invented, and dp_overlay_fault and the geneve_overlay_dp_counters class depend on them.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the NSX 4.2 ESXi CLI reference for real datapath drop/encap counters (for example the nsxdp-cli commands documented for 4.x) and rename the fields, or remove the overlay counter branch.

findings.explanation: 'esxcli network nic stats get' reports totals such as packets, bytes, dropped, total receive/transmit errors, CRC, frame, FIFO and missed errors. It has no pause-frame, alignment, tail-drop or noBuffer counters; those come only from driver-private statistics (vsish/ethtool-style) and vary by NIC vendor. The 'vsipfwwd watchdog' explanation for these counters is also unsupported.
findings.quote: emitting JSON keys for rx_errors, tx_errors, rx_drops, tx_drops, fcs_errors, crc_errors, alignment_errors, pause_frames_rx, tail_drop_count, noBuffer_count
findings.suggested_fix: Map fields to the actual esxcli output names, and mark pause/tail-drop/noBuffer as optional driver-specific counters with the command that exposes them.

findings.explanation: GET /api/v1/transport-nodes returns configuration and inventory, not per-vmnic error or drop counters. The SPL still searches vmware:nsxt:transport_node for rx_errors/fcs_errors, so that half of the search will normally contribute nothing.
findings.quote: **`vmware:nsxt:transport_node`** snapshots sourced from **`GET /api/v1/transport-nodes`** Policy or Manager REST pulls plus nested NIC inventories where exported
findings.suggested_fix: Say that error counters come only from the esxi:nic:stats collector (or per-node interface stats APIs, if verified), and that transport_node is used only for identity enrichment.

findings.explanation: Granting Enterprise Administrator contradicts least privilege and the grounding guide, which says the read-only Auditor role is enough for collectors.
findings.quote: Limit collectors to **`Auditor`** plus tightly scoped **`Enterprise Administrator`** privileges

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware documents sourcetypes such as vmware:events, vmware:tasks and vmware:inv:*. 'vmware:vc:event' and 'vmware:vmware:vsphere:vcenter' do not look like its names, and 'vmware:esxi:syslog' does not match the ESXi Logs add-on sourcetypes.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Splunk Add-on for VMware and the ESXi Logs add-on sourcetype tables, and use the real names.

findings.explanation: NSX requires an underlay MTU of at least 1600 (1700 recommended). It does not lower guest MTU to 1450, so a 1500 underlay is a misconfiguration that causes drops, not a defined 'inner ceiling'.
findings.quote: highlighting GENEVE inner **`1450`** ceilings whenever `physical` **`MTU`** stays **`1500`**
findings.suggested_fix: Say that a TEP uplink MTU below 1600 (VMware recommends 1700) is a misconfiguration, and flag it as such.

findings.explanation: The SPL outputs no rack_id, transport_node, tail_drop_num or pause_frames_rx; it outputs tn_key, peak_tail_drop and peak_pause_rx.
findings.quote: (1) Heat-map: **`rack_id`** versus **`peak_crc`**/**`peak_fcs`** per **`vmnic`**. (2) Matrix: **`transport_node`** × **`nic_key`** coloring **`tail_drop_num`** versus **`pause_frames_rx`**.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the SPL's output names (tn_key, peak_tail_drop, peak_pause_rx) and note that rack_id needs a CMDB lookup.

findings.explanation: The title names a specific KB but the link is the KB portal root. docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-NSX has also been retired in favour of techdocs.broadcom.com.
findings.quote:
"title": "VMware KB — Verify ESXi NIC statistics and duplex settings",
      "url": "https://knowledge.broadcom.com/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the specific Broadcom KB article and the techdocs NSX 4.2 pages.

findings.explanation: NIC error counters are not flow records, so Network_Traffic does not fit, and the SPL uses no datamodel.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop Network_Traffic; keep Performance (Network dataset) only if counters are actually mapped.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an agent, and the collection design (UF on ESXi, netcpa counters) could not work as written. There is no sign of SME validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft until an SME has validated the collector and the SPL on real hosts.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: esxcli NIC statistics are cumulative since driver load, but the SPL sums and thresholds them as if they were per-poll deltas (composite_fault>0, sum_rx_errors). Any NIC that ever logged one error alerts on every run, and sums over 15 minutes inflate with poll frequency. Compute per-poll deltas first (streamstats current=f last() BY tn_key nic_key), then threshold.

The streamstats window=4 avg(sum_rx_errors) includes the current row (default current=t), so rx_jump compares the value against an average that already contains it, which damps real jumps. Use current=f.

The nsxt_* overlay counter fields and the pause/tail-drop/noBuffer fields are not confirmed in any documented esxcli or nsxdp-cli output. Check the source names before relying on the geneve_overlay_dp_counters and ring_tail_drop_burst classes.

summary: Watching per-vmnic errors and drops under the NSX overlay is a useful idea, and the UC correctly cites Splunk_TA_vmware as 3215. However, the NSX app ID is wrong, the collection design runs Universal Forwarder scripts on ESXi (not a supported platform), and it relies on 'nsxdp-cli netcpa' counters that do not match current NSX tooling. The SPL also treats cumulative NIC counters as per-interval values, so any NIC with a historical error stays alerting.
